result.topic_en: Bare calculations, written upside down relative to the scan, on partial derivatives and variations of quantities built from (a-b)^2/r^2 and (a+b)^2/r'^2, with logarithmic substitutions, apparently part of Riemann's equations of motion for a rotating fluid ellipsoid.
result.transcription:
$\frac{(a-b)^2}{r^2}+\frac{(a+b)^2}{r'^2} - \varkappa$
$2\frac{(a-b)^2}{r^2}+\frac{(a+b)^2}{r'^2} = \frac{2}{\iota}\left(\frac{\partial\log\alpha}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial\log\beta}{\partial x}\right)[?] = -\frac{2}{\iota}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$ [?]
$2\frac{(a-b)^2}{r^2}+\frac{(a+b)^2}{r'^2} = -\frac{\iota}{\iota}\left(\frac{\partial\log\alpha}{\partial x}\frac{\partial\log\beta}{\partial x}\right) = -\frac{2}{\iota}\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}$ [?]
$\frac{\partial p}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial\log\alpha}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial\log\beta}{\partial x}$ [?]
$\log\alpha = \varphi+\psi+const$ [?]
$\log\beta = \varphi-\psi+const$ [?]
$\delta(x,\iota)\,6\,\frac{(a-b)^4}{r^2}(\delta a-\delta b)^2+\frac{(a+b)^4}{r'^2}(\delta a+\delta b)^2$ [?]
$4\frac{(a-b)^2}{r^2} = -\frac{2}{\iota}\left(\frac{\partial\log\alpha}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial\log\beta}{\partial x}\right)+\frac{\iota}{\iota}\frac{\partial\log\alpha}{\partial x}\frac{\partial\log\beta}{\partial x}$ [?]
$4\frac{(a+b)^2}{r'^2} = -\frac{2}{\iota}\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}\right)+\frac{a}{\iota}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$ [?]
$\frac{b-a}{\iota}+\frac{b+a}{\iota}$
$\frac{b-a}{\iota}+\frac{b+a}{\iota} = \frac{2b}{(b^2-a^2)}$ [?]
$\delta\varkappa = \frac{2}{3}(\delta a^2+\delta b^2)\left(-\frac{b^2-a^2}{\iota}\ldots\right)$ [?]
$\delta^2 q = 6\frac{(a-b)^4}{r^2}(\delta a-\delta b)^2+\frac{(a+b)^4}{r'^2}(\delta a+\delta b)^2$ [?]
$4\frac{(a-b)^2}{r^2} = -\frac{2}{\iota}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}+\frac{a}{\iota}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$ [?]
$4\frac{(a+b)^2}{r'^2} = -\frac{2}{\iota}\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}-\frac{a}{\iota}\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}$ [?]
$\frac{b-a}{\iota}\quad\frac{b+a}{\iota}$
$2\frac{(a-b)^4}{r^2}+\frac{(a+b)^4}{r'^2} = \ldots$ [?]
$2\frac{(a+b)^2}{r'^2}-2\frac{(b-a)^2}{r^2} = \ldots\frac{a(b^2-a^2)}{\iota}\frac{\partial \varkappa}{\partial x}$ [?]
$\delta q = -(b^2-a^2)\left(\frac{\partial\varkappa}{\partial x}\ldots\right)$ [?]
$+3(\delta a^2\delta x^2+\ldots)$ [?]
$\delta x = \delta q - dp$
$dx = 2q\,dp$ [?]
$[-\ldots-]$
$\frac{\partial \varkappa}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial \varkappa}{\partial x} = \frac{\iota}{\iota}\left(\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\right)\,a\,\delta q^2 - 2a\,\delta p\,\delta q+(a^2-4\iota+\iota^2)\delta p^2$ [?]
$2a\frac{\partial\varkappa}{\partial x}-2\frac{\partial\varkappa}{\partial x} = \left(a\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}(a^2-4\iota^2)\right)(\ldots\delta p(\delta q-dp))$ [?]
$-(b^2-a^2)\left(\frac{\partial\varkappa}{\partial x}\,dq^2+2\,dp\,dq\ldots\right)$ [?]
$\varkappa = \frac{1}{\iota}q$ [?]
$\frac{\partial p}{\partial x} = \frac{1}{\iota}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$
$\frac{\partial p}{\partial x} = \frac{1}{\iota}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}-\frac{1}{\iota}q$ [?]
$\frac{\partial \varkappa}{\partial x} = \frac{1}{\iota}\left(\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}-q\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}+4q\right)$ [?]
$\frac{\partial p\partial q}{\partial x^2} = \frac{1}{\iota}\left(\frac{\partial p\partial q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}\right)$ [?]
$-(b^2-a^2)\frac{\partial\varkappa}{\partial q}\delta q$ [?]
$+\frac{2}{\iota}\left(\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}+4q\right)a\,\delta q^2+2\,\delta p\,\delta q\left(\frac{2}{\iota}a\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}-2q\right)+\frac{2}{\iota}\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}(a^2-4\iota^2)$ [?]
$+4(b^2-a^2)\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$ [?]
$+\delta p^2\left(\frac{2}{\iota}a\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}+(a^2-4\iota^2)\left(\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}-2q\right)\frac{2}{\iota}\right)$ [?]

methods.what: Logarithmic parametrisation of auxiliary quantities alpha, beta, gamma by new variables p, q
Partial derivatives of log alpha and log beta with respect to the variables
Second-order Taylor expansion (variation) of q in terms of variations of x and p
